description: Round-7 audit: confirmed --compile-check false-READY fixtures. Each is a document the CLI reports READY (exit 0) but pdflatex rejects under the strict READY oracle. The monotone gate (scripts/tools/check_known_false_ready.py) runs the CLI only (no TeX) and fails if any fixed fixture regresses or a live false-READY appears where none was recorded. Each R7 fix PR flips its entries' expected_cli to NOT-READY and lowers the baseline. Ground truth verified locally against pdflatex; refresh/verify with scripts/tools/false_ready_oracle.sh.
ready_oracle: clean single pass with no LaTeX Error (docs/COMPILATION_GUARANTEE.md SO1). strong-fatal = pdflatex produces NO PDF even under nonstopmode; error-halt = fails -halt-on-error / emits a LaTeX Error but limps to a PDF under nonstopmode.

There is NO duplicated declaration and no visible mistake -- the author loads a package and declares theorems the ordinary way, which is why the class survives review. THE WILD-TYPE FORM: the first real-paper differential (corpora/real_roots) found 8 of 11 false-READYs in a 200-paper arXiv sample are this \c@<env> class, making it the largest single source of false-READY on real documents. false-READY visible only on the SECOND pdflatex run: \addcontentsline writes a raw token into .toc, which \tableofcontents reads on the NEXT run. Unlike .aux (which \enddocument re-inputs in the same run, latex.ltx:15483-15489) the .toc is never re-read by its writer, so a document can poison only its successor. The tool models .aux and not .toc.

NATURAL form of the .toc second-pass hazard: a macro defined in the BODY and used in a \section title. \section writes the title unexpanded into .toc; \tableofcontents reads it on the NEXT run before the definition has executed. pass 1 rc 0 + PDF, pass 2 rc 1.

blank line (TeX \par) inside a math range: '! Missing $ inserted.' Affects $..$, \(..\), \[..\] and amsmath envs alike. A comment-only line is NOT a \par and compiles, so a detector must be comment-aware.

M1 breaker (OPEN-007): \lstnewenvironment body is verbatim to TeX but the env is not in the scanner's 11-name verbatim_envs, so naive %-to-EOL blanking blanks '% <U+8868>' (bytes [118,123)) inside the body and hides the live fatal ('! LaTeX Error: Invalid UTF-8 byte sequence' via listings; halt rc 1,1). Blanked variant: CLI READY = manufactured false-READY. A comment-aware fix must treat % inside CUSTOM verbatim envs as literal; a wrong one flips this to READY and check_known_false_ready fails REGRESSION.

M2 breaker: '\begin {verbatim}' with a SPACE — the vcu scanner's starts_with "\begin{" is offset-exact, but TeX absorbs the space and the env IS verbatim ('! Unicode character U+8868'; halt rc 1,1). Naive blanking blanks '% <U+8868>' (bytes [72,77)) and the T3 japanese_cjk reason DISAPPEARS; exit stays NOT-READY today only because T0 shares the same space-blindness (Unexpected \end{document} + PRT-001) — right answer by accident, and T0 over-rejects the compiling plain-body sibling (rc 0,0). When T0 learns the space form this fixture becomes the exit-level kill-test; until then the kill signal is reason-level (T3 must keep firing).

M3 breaker: LETTER \verb delimiter (\verb aQ%<U+8868>a) is legal TeX — the Unicode-character error proves 'a' delimited and '%' literal (halt rc 1,1). The scanner's is_letter guard records NO range, so naive blanking blanks '%<U+8868>a after' (bytes [56,67)) and hides the fatal. Blanked variant: CLI READY = manufactured false-READY.

M4 breaker, literal spelling: \catcode`\%=12 makes '%<U+8868> after' live body text ('! Unicode character U+8868'; halt rc 1,1). Naive blanking blanks bytes [63,73) and hides the CJK, but T0's LP-Foreign \catcode guard keeps exit NOT-READY — masked at exit level (kill signal is the T3 reason). See fr_cmt_m4b_percent_ignore for the unmasked vector.

M4 breaker, unmasked vector: doc.sty \MakePercentIgnore sets catcode`\%=9 with NO literal \catcode (wild-type: every .dtx driver), so LP-Foreign does not fire; '%<U+8868> after' is live ('! Unicode character U+8868'; halt rc 1,1). Naive blanking blanks bytes [84,94) -> CLI READY = manufactured false-READY.

Over-blank guard (the OTHER wrong implementation): CJK inside a correctly-spelled verbatim env is LIVE ('! Unicode character U+8868'; halt rc 1,1). Blanking the FULL find_verbatim_comment_url_ranges set — the untagged (int*int) list misreading, revert #1's alltt/listing mechanism, OPEN-007's measured 11 manufactured false-READYs — blanks the whole env body (bytes [48,91)) -> CLI READY. Comment-only blanking blanks NOTHING here (measured: zero ranges) and must stay NOT-READY.

TARGET (d): raw CJK only in a trailing mid-line %-comment (OPEN-007's wild shape, '\vspace{-0.05cm} % <CJK>'). pdflatex rc 0,0 both protocols with PDF; today NOT-READY via T3 japanese_cjk (comment-blind has_raw_cjk — bytes [67,102) are a genuine comment). The comment-awareness fix flips expected_cli to READY in the same PR. LANDING CAVEAT: false_ready_oracle.sh hard-fails ANY grade=compiles; extend its comparator to accept manifest-recorded 'compiles' first (one line at the HARD-drift branch). FLIPPED by the OPEN-007 comment-awareness fix (2026-09-01): the trailing mid-line CJK comment is blanked before feature detection, so Japanese_cjk no longer fires; READY now matches pdflatex (compiles). Accept-pin: a NOT-READY here is a rescue regression.

TARGET (e): fully commented-out '% \usepackage{fontspec}' (bytes [24,47), a genuine comment). pdflatex rc 0,0 both protocols with PDF; today NOT-READY via T3 opentype_fonts (comment-blind uses_package). Fix flips to READY. Same oracle-comparator caveat as fr_cmt_target_cjk_comment.
